L20: # Replayable Authority Histories for Auditing Automated Agents
L21: ## 【0†Abstract】
L22: Software agents act on authority that changes while they run: permissions are granted and revoked, running instances are replaced, and some requests are refused. Activity logs record what a system reports it did, but they do not by themselves show what an agent was allowed to do when it acted, and the operator can edit them.
L23: This document specifies a model for an authority history: an append-only, signed record of who granted what to whom, which actions were admitted, which requests were refused, and which unfinished duties survive when one agent replaces another. Given independently authenticated owner keys and history identity, a verifier can replay the history and recompute its recorded authorization decisions while trusting neither the agent nor the operator.
L24: The document states what such a verifier can and cannot establish. Optional profiles cover external anchoring, federated operation, human-attested keys and zero-knowledge disclosure. An informative appendix describes one encoding.【1†¶】
